clue.text: Instructional text used in preparation of course

definitions.text: Instructional text used in preparation of course

parts.words: Instructional text used in preparation of course
parts.note: surface reading: a teaching handout used while preparing a course of study
setter's reading: the course is a course of a meal, and the text tells a cook how to make it

explanation.surface: A teacher's handout used while planning an academic course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests education, but it means a dish served at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookery card or page of written steps for making a dish is exactly what a cook follows in the kitchen.

clue.text: Rocky situation faced, so to speak, by four presidents?

definitions.text: Rocky situation faced, so to speak, by four presidents?

parts.note: surface reading: a difficult predicament confronting four heads of state

parts.words: faced, so to speak, by four presidents
parts.note: setter's reading: a mountain whose rock is literally carved with four presidents' faces

explanation.surface: Four presidents confront a precarious crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' means made of rock and 'faced' means bearing carved faces: Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt and Lincoln in South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Dakota mountain carved with four colossal heads of US presidents is a famous granite monument.

clue.text: Make more crude, disturbing a censor

indicators.note: disturbing something knocks it out of place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Adding vulgarity to a film would upset the censor.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen something is to make it rougher or more vulgar, a verb matching the defining phrase.

clue.text: King on one vessel captured by noble warship

indicators.note: something captured by another is held inside it

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one
a vat is a large container

explanation.surface: A king aboard a ship is taken prisoner by an aristocrat's man-of-war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship but here it is a tub; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned armed ship licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Off-putting statement from me as pagan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., what a procrastinator says when putting a task off
second meaning: a worshipper of idols

explanation.surface: Someone's discouraging remark marks them out as a heathen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-putting' looks like 'unpleasant', but it means postponing: split the answer as I DO LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol-worshipper follows gods other than the established faith, so is a heathen or pagan.

clue.text: Removing forces from a revolt after limited changes

indicators.note: after says the piece before it in the clue is placed second, behind what follows
when something changes its form is altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a rising is a rebellion

explanation.surface: Troops are withdrawn following an uprising once some restricted reforms are made.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a participle phrase; 'from' belongs to it rather than to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking military troops and installations out of an area is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Old money from Europe, including British pound

indicators.note: something including another holds it within its letters

parts.note: the lira was Italy's currency before the euro
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A former European currency once included the British pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like part of the British money, but it alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra was the Roman pound weight, which is why lb is the abbreviation for pound.

clue.text: Form of instruction can, when a head is included

indicators.note: something that is included goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a tin is a can
a head means per person, which is each

explanation.surface: A teaching method works when a headteacher is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' means per head, as in prices quoted at five pounds a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal series of lectures and discussions on a topical subject, a type of teaching session.

clue.text: One can count on it as a devotional aid

definitions.text: One can count on it as a devotional aid

parts.note: surface reading: something dependable you can rely on
setter's reading: literally counting prayers on a string of beads

explanation.surface: Something reliable that helps people in their worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' means rely on, but here it is literal: the beads keep a tally of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholics use a string of beads to keep count of Hail Marys and other prayers recited in sequence.

clue.text: Objected about perhaps changing drug taken the wrong way

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round what follows

parts.note: if you minded something, you objected to it

indicators.note: a word that is changing takes a different form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone protested that a drug, maybe a changed one, had been swallowed incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' suggests swallowing a drug, but here it means understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To misapprehend is to misunderstand, so something misapprehended has been understood wrongly.

clue.text: Is included in list man arranged — as a rule, it was awful

indicators.note: something included in another thing sits inside it, so one group of letters goes within the other
letters that are arranged are put into a new order rather than the given one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's jumbled list contains something, and some regime was dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' at the start looks like a verb, but it is fodder; the definition is the cryptic tail describing a brutal regime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator's system of government was a notoriously brutal form of rule.

clue.text: Runs into singer and part of orchestra

indicators.note: something that runs into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a vocalist and a section of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpets, trombones, horns and tubas make up the brass section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Cosmetic mother applied over a mark on skin

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
a scar is a mark left on the skin by a wound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum puts make-up over a blemish to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is the make-up brushed onto eyelashes, one of the standard cosmetics.

clue.text: Article penned by humorous author for kid, say

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed as if in a pen, so it goes inside

parts.note: Edward Lear, the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: A comic writer produces a piece for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child, but it is kid leather made from young goatskin; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is a soft type of goatskin, so it is an example of tanned hide.

clue.text: Appliance for cooking fruit missing front ring

indicators.note: missing its front means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget for cooking fruit has lost its front hob ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is the letter O, and it is the front of the fruit that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with an oven and hotplates, used for cooking.

clue.text: Make a contribution with good setting up

parts.note: to pitch in is to contribute or join in
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone offers a contribution while being good about setting things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitching a tent or a stall means erecting it, so it is a synonym for putting it up.

clue.text: Male with cunning thought sincere

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
art can mean craft or cunning
to feel is to believe, so thought gives felt

explanation.surface: A crafty man believed himself honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings come from the heart, so they are genuine and sincerely meant.

clue.text: Visualised a drink in dime novel

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
novel means new, so the word is given a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A reader pictured a drink scene in a cheap pulp thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: A dime novel is a cheap American pulp story; here 'novel' is split off as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form a picture of it in the mind, so the two past tenses match.

clue.text: Person supervising old English writing, perhaps, including poetry

indicators.note: a word that includes something holds it inside its own letters

parts.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry
writing is one of the three Rs, so R can stand for it

explanation.surface: A supervisor oversees old English writing that includes some poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'writing, perhaps' is one R.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer is a foreman or manager who watches over the work of others.

clue.text: Sour stuff very shortly happening, with anger rising

indicators.note: shortly says the preceding word is abbreviated to a single letter

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
in means fashionable or happening

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Something bitter is about to occur as fury mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is an acidic liquid, the archetypal sour-tasting condiment.

clue.text: Alternative to reveille in Territorial Army

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers have some other way of waking up than the bugle.
explanation.walkthrough: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing clock that rouses a sleeper does the same job as the morning bugle call in a barracks.

clue.text: Leaders leaving bar aid city that's showing effect of drought

indicators.note: the leaders are the opening letters, and they leave, so each word loses its first letter

parts.note: bar without its first letter
aid without its first letter
city without its first letter

explanation.surface: Politicians are quitting a city blocked from aid during a dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjectival phrase read loosely as a noun: the state shown by drought.
explanation.definitionFit: Aridity is extreme dryness, the condition a long drought leaves behind.

clue.text: Flower-girl turned up with American star

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Iris is both a flower and a girl's name
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A flower seller arrived with a famous American celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: I belong with new organisation in base

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: giving something a new organisation sets it out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are a member of a new organisation at its headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a headquarters, but it is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and the answer are both adjectives for something mean, dishonourable or lacking in moral worth.

clue.text: Staff don't make declaration

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short stick, such as a conductor's or relay runner's
second meaning: read as ..., carry on batting in cricket instead of declaring the innings closed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare, ending the team's innings early; to bat on is to keep batting instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a stick or rod, and staff is an old word for a stick carried in the hand.

clue.text: Being portrayed as smart about use of computers

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to smart is to sting
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Someone shown as clever with computer use.
explanation.definitionFit: A person posing for a painter is said to be sitting for their portrait, the moment of being depicted.

clue.text: Form of gold or silver used in helping others

indicators.note: letters used in a phrase are found inside it, running across the words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Precious metal put to use helping other people.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast bar or block of metal, the standard form for storing bullion.

clue.text: Weed found in land, one I'd destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so its letters are left in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a weed on their land and has destroyed it.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow-flowered plant with fluffy seed heads is a common lawn and garden weed.

clue.text: After partner's heart, play this

parts.note: surface reading: following the middle letter of a word, as in letter games
setter's reading: a suitor who is after (seeking) someone's affection plays this music to them

explanation.surface: An instruction to play something once a partner's heart has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' means pursuing, not following in sequence; 'heart' is affection, not a middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Music sung or played beneath a beloved's window to woo them is the classic romantic gesture.

clue.text: Didn't go steady, being fickle

indicators.note: something fickle keeps changing, so its letters will not hold their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stopped dating their sweetheart because they were inconstant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go steady' looks like one phrase about dating, but 'Didn't go' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where you are is the opposite of leaving, so the past tense means did not depart.
